correctness.rationale: All quantifiers a,b>=1, t>=2 and arbitrary marker set are handled: for factor length >=p, p-spaced occurrences have overlapping intervals covering every internal 10 boundary; for smaller factors, unary factors embed in a covered maximal run, mixed factors containing 10 are periodically relocated to a selected internal 10, and remaining mixed factors are 0^r1^s relocated to a selected 01. This proves the four-factor iff test. Explicit witness marker sets prove irredundance within the four tests. A mandatory two-letter lower bound and exhaustive classification of two-position markers yield the 2t(t-1), (t-1)(bt+1), and (t-1)(at+1) counts, with a=b=1 agreeing. The independent direct-factor checker compares 330960 position subsets across 37 parameter triples; 150 parameter triples independently check counts. No finite sample substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: String-attractor membership normally requires checking all distinct factors or running a general verification algorithm. An exact list of only four factor constraints, valid for arbitrary candidate marker sets throughout a three-parameter infinite word family, is a genuine structural simplification. Its irredundance has a sharp singleton-run boundary, and its complete all-size-two classification yields exact polynomial populations with another boundary at min(a,b)=1. These quantities are directly motivated by 2026 studies of minimum-attractor multiplicities and factor-coverage certificates. The claim is not merely the known gamma=2 observation, a special-case table, or a routine normalization.
